ei.title: Chapter 1-04 1번: Our Actions as Social Performances
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: There is something in human nature that prompts us to think of our actions, as well as our feelings, as though they were the distinctive issue of something inside us, something uniquely ours. Some are. But most of the actions and feelings that help us enter into working relations with fellow members of the world are not all that private. They are, in fact, performances we execute in acceptably close conformity to widely accepted social rules. These rules are learned and held by us in such an easy way that we indulge the conceit that they are our own brilliant accomplishments. We think of them as though they were the inventions of our own utterly original psychic lives, when most of them are as familiar to others as they are to us. Social things are quite simply social.

questions.passage: There is something in human nature that prompts us to think of our actions, as well as our feelings, as though they were the (A)[distinctive / ordinary] issue of something inside us, something uniquely ours. Some are. But most of the actions and feelings that help us enter into working relations with fellow members of the world are not all that (B)[private / public]. They are, in fact, performances we execute in acceptably close (C)[conformity / resistance] to widely accepted social rules. These rules are learned and held by us in such an easy way that we indulge the conceit that they are our own brilliant accomplishments. We think of them as though they were the inventions of our own utterly original psychic lives, when most of them are as familiar to others as they are to us. Social things are quite simply social.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 우리의 행동이 독특한(distinctive) 산물이라고 생각하지만, 대부분은 사적인(private) 것이 아니며, 사회 규칙에 대한 순응(conformity)에 따라 수행된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① distinctive — private — conformity — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② ordinary — private — conformity (A 반대: 독특한→평범한)
❌ ③ distinctive — public — conformity (B 반대: 사적인→공적인)
❌ ④ distinctive — private — resistance (C 반대: 순응→저항)

questions.passage: There is something in human nature that (A)[prompts / prevents] us to think of our actions, as well as our feelings, as though they were the distinctive issue of something inside us, something uniquely ours. Some are. But most of the actions and feelings that help us enter into working relations with fellow members of the world are not all that private. They are, in fact, performances we (B)[execute / abandon] in acceptably close conformity to widely accepted social rules. These rules are learned and held by us in such an easy way that we indulge the conceit that they are our own brilliant (C)[accomplishments / failures]. We think of them as though they were the inventions of our own utterly original psychic lives, when most of them are as familiar to others as they are to us. Social things are quite simply social.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 인간 본성이 우리를 촉구하고(prompts), 수행하며(execute), 우리의 훌륭한 업적(accomplishments)이라고 자만한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① prevents — execute — accomplishments (A 반대: 촉구하다→막다)
❌ ② prompts — abandon — accomplishments (B 반대: 수행하다→포기하다)
❌ ③ prompts — execute — failures (C 반대: 업적→실패)
✅ ④ prompts — execute — accomplishments — 원문 일치 ←정답

questions.passage: There is something in human nature that prompts us to think of our actions, as well as our feelings, as though they were the distinctive issue of something inside us, something uniquely ours. They are, in fact, performances we execute in acceptably close conformity to widely accepted social rules. We think of them as though they were the inventions of our own (C)[utterly / slightly] original psychic lives, when most of them are as familiar to others as they are to us. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 우리는 자만심에 빠지고(indulge the conceit), 완전히(utterly) 독창적인 정신적 삶의 발명품이라고 생각한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① suppress — conceit — utterly (A 반대: 빠지다→억누르다)
✅ ② indulge — conceit — utterly — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ indulge — humility — utterly (B 반대: 자만심→겸손)
❌ ④ indulge — conceit — slightly (C 반대: 완전히→약간)

Some are. But most of the actions and feelings that help us ③<u>break off</u> working relations with fellow members of the world are not all that private. They are, in fact, performances we execute in acceptably close ④<u>conformity</u> to widely accepted social rules. These rules are learned and held by us in such an easy way that we indulge the conceit that they are our own brilliant accomplishments. We think of them as though they were the inventions of our own utterly original psychic lives, when most of them are as familiar to others as they are to us. Social things are quite simply social.

det.korean: '끊다(break off)'가 아니라 '관계를 맺다(enter into)'가 문맥상 적절하다.

① prompts — 촉구하다, 원문 일치
② distinctive — 독특한, 원문 일치
③ break off — 원문은 enter into(관계를 맺다) ←정답
④ conformity — 순응, 원문 일치
det.tip: enter into(관계를 맺다) ↔ break off(끊다, 단절하다)
